cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, and they skip the warm-up completely: "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain." No small talk, friend. Straight to the praise.

Then they start bragging on that mountain: Mount Zion is beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon. They talk about it the way I talk about a tray of cookies fresh out of the oven, and friend, I do NOT stop talking.

cards.question: The song gives Mount Zion one more title. Whose city does it call Zion?

cards.text: Zion's got citadels, the strongholds of the city. And the song tells you exactly who's in them.

cards.question: The song says God is in Zion's citadels and has shown Himself to be a fortress.

cards.text: Then this: "For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together." Not one king, friend, a whole CROWD of kings, and I'd be checking every lock on the bakery door.

cards.question: The kings get close enough to see God's city. They are astounded, and they ___ in terror.

cards.text: Trembling seizes them right there, anguish like a woman in labor. I know that tremble, friend: every time the junk drawer opened, I shook just like that, and all anybody wanted was the scissors.

cards.question: Then the song speaks right to God about the ships of Tarshish. What does it say God wrecked them with?

cards.text: Everybody's ordered something that looked amazing in the picture, then opened the box and went, "Oh. Oh no." The people had heard all about God's city, and now they say how it stacks up.

cards.question: The people had heard about the city of the LORD of Hosts. What do they say about it now?

answers.text: They have seen it for themselves
It was only an old story
They are still waiting to see it

cards.question: In that same line, the people say what God will do for His city: God will establish her ___.

cards.text: Kings ran, ships sank, and now the song gets quiet and goes within God's temple. The people slow down there and think about one thing.

cards.question: Within God's temple, what do the people contemplate?
The song tells God that His name reaches only as far as Zion's walls.

cards.text: His name goes to the ends of the earth, and the song says His right hand is full of righteousness. Then Mount Zion is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice right along with it.

cards.question: Mount Zion is glad and the daughters of Judah rejoice on account of God's ___.

cards.text: Then the song gives an order: "March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers," then consider her ramparts and tour her citadels. This psalm wants you to get your steps in, friend, and I've been stuck on a gold base my whole life, so I'm HOPPING that lap.

cards.question: Why does the song say to walk around Zion counting towers and touring citadels?

answers.text: To report back to the king

cards.text: Then the last line: "For this God is our God forever and ever;" Friend, I got swapped out once for a shinier stamper, so trust me, FOREVER and ever is the best news in this whole song.

cards.question: The song's last line says this God will be their guide. For how long?

findings.problem: The sons of Korah show up for the first time, but the card never says who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card spends words defining "citadels" ("the strongholds of the city") instead of leaving it to the dictionary pop-up.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The joke is about something that looked great in a picture but disappointed when it arrived. Verse 8 is the opposite: what the people heard is exactly what they saw. The comparison doesn't share the core action, and it points the baker toward the wrong answer "It was only an old story" on card 11.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line "God will establish her ___." Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward "forever" over "again" or "soon," so it tests unseen wording instead of meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Stop 2's question types run multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, multiple choice, multiple choice. That repeats the first five cards of stop 1's pattern exactly.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "I've been stuck on a gold base my whole life" adds something new to his backstory and contradicts it. He only got the gold base when he was renewed in the Dorinverse, and the base never sticks him in place, because he can hop and jump with it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
